chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Bashir al-Nabbal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about fasting on the day of doubt. So he said: Fast it. For if it be from Sha'ban, it would be a voluntary fast, and if it be from the Month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which you were granted success.

key_terms.تَطَوُّع: Voluntary/supererogatory act of worship; a fast performed beyond obligation
key_terms.وُفِّقْتَ: You were granted tawfiq (divine success/alignment); a positive framing meaning God guided you to observe Ramadan correctly
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: The 'day of doubt' — the last day of Sha'ban when there is uncertainty about whether Ramadan has begun

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the day of doubt (yawm al-shakk) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) gives a ruling on the 'day of doubt' (yawm al-shakk) — the last day of Sha'ban when there is uncertainty about whether the new moon of Ramadan has been sighted. He instructs that one should fast on this day: if it turns out to be the last day of Sha'ban, the fast counts as a voluntary (nafl) fast; if it turns out to be the first day of Ramadan, then one has been divinely guided to observe it. This hadith reflects the Imami jurisprudential principle of erring on the side of worship, while framing the ambiguous day as an opportunity for divine tawfiq (success/guidance).

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Al Suhban, from Muhammad Bin Bakr Bin Janah, from Ali Bin Shajara, from Bashir Al Nabbal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Fast of the day of doubt. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast it. So, if it was from Shaban, it was a voluntary (Fast), and if it was from the Month of Ramazan, so it would be a commensurate day for it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ibn abu al-Suhban from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah from Ali ibn Shajarah from Bashir al-Nabbal who has said the following: “I once asked Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a doubtful day.
He (the Imam) said, ’Fast on such day, if it is of al-Sha £ ban, it is optional and if it is of the month of Ramadan then it is a day in which you have a fortunate chance.’”
